about.title: Eight and nine
about.length_note: About 10 minutes. There are two new numbers, and each gets its own short stretch of frames, real things and a few questions. You can stop after the 8 part or after the 9 part and pick up later.

say.text: Welcome back. Today we meet two new numbers: eight and nine. There is no rush. You can stop at any point and come back later.
First, a quick look at something you know. This is a five-frame: a row of five boxes. Every box has a dot in it. The frame is full. How many dots? Five.

show.text: A single row of 5 square boxes, each with one big dot. The whole row is filled.

ask.q: How many dots are in this full frame?
ask.why: Every one of the five boxes has a dot, so the full frame is five.

say.text: Now we put a second five-frame next to the first. Two frames side by side. Together they have ten boxes. We won't fill them all today. We will use them to build eight and nine.

show.text: Two rows of 5 boxes side by side. The left frame is full of dots. The right frame is empty.

say.text: To make eight, keep the left frame full. That is five. Now add three dots in the second frame. Five and three more makes eight.

show.text: Left frame: 5 dots, full. Right frame: 3 dots in the first three boxes, 2 boxes empty.

say.text: Let's count them one at a time. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. Eight. Say it with me if you like: eight.
Look at this picture. The left frame is full, and the right frame has three dots. How many dots altogether?

show.text: Left frame: 5 dots. Right frame: 3 dots and 2 empty boxes.

ask.q: How many dots are there altogether?
ask.why: Five in the full frame and three more make eight. There are two empty boxes in the second frame.

say.text: Now real things. Imagine eight cups on a table, five in one row and three in another. For a child, it could be eight ducks in a line. You can see five and three straight away, and you know it is eight.

show.text: A table with 8 cups: a row of 5 and a row of 3 below it. Beside it, 8 yellow ducks in the same pattern.

ask.q: How many cups are on the table?
ask.why: A row of five and a row of three make eight.

say.text: Now nine. Keep the left frame full, that is five. This time add four dots in the second frame. Five and four more makes nine.

show.text: Left frame: 5 dots, full. Right frame: 4 dots and 1 empty box at the end.

say.text: Count: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. Nine. Say it with me: nine.
See the one empty box? Two frames hold ten. Nine fills all but one box. So nine is one away from ten. That empty box is a handy clue.
Try this one. The left frame is full. The right frame has four dots and one empty box.

show.text: Left frame: 5 dots. Right frame: 4 dots and 1 empty box.

ask.why: Five and four make nine. Ten would fill every box, and one box is empty.

say.text: Nine real things. Imagine nine keys, five on one row and four on another. Or nine apples for a child, in the same pattern. One space is left over, just like the empty box.

show.text: A table with 9 keys: a row of 5 and a row of 4 below it. Beside it, 9 red apples in the same pattern.

ask.q: How many keys are on the table?
ask.why: A row of five and a row of four make nine.

say.text: Now the written numbers. This is the digit 8, said eight. It looks like two loops, one on top of the other. This is the digit 9, said nine. It has one loop at the top and a tail that goes down.

show.text: Left: the digit 8, said 'eight', two loops stacked. Right: the digit 9, said 'nine', a loop with a tail going down.

say.text: If you like, trace each digit in the air with your finger and say its name. We will practise writing properly in the next class, so there is no pressure today.

show.text: Trace 8 and say 'eight'. Trace 9 and say 'nine'. Writing comes next class.

say.text: Here are two frames. Only one has an empty box left over in the second frame. Look closely.

show.text: Two pictures. Picture 1: left frame full, right frame has 3 dots and 2 empty boxes. Picture 2: left frame full, right frame has 4 dots and 1 empty box.

ask.q: Which picture has just one empty box, so it shows nine?
ask.right: Picture 2, with four dots in the second frame
wrong: Picture 1, with three dots in the second frame
ask.why: Nine is five and four. That leaves only one empty box. Picture 1 has two empty boxes, so it shows eight.

say.text: Now a mix of numbers from nothing up to nine. Here are some coins on a table, five in one row and one more below.

show.text: 6 coins: a row of 5 and 1 coin below.

ask.why: A full row of five and one more make six.

say.text: Next, a table with no cups on it at all. Or a pond with no ducks.

show.text: An empty table. Nothing on it.

ask.q: How many cups are on the table?
ask.why: Nothing is there, so the number is zero.

say.text: One more. Nine ducks are in a pond, five in a row and four in another row.

show.text: 9 ducks on a pond: a row of 5 and a row of 4.

ask.q: How many ducks are in the pond?
ask.why: Five and four make nine. One more duck would make ten.

say.text: Well done. Today you saw eight as a full frame and three more. You saw nine as a full frame and four more, with one empty box. You can stop here. Next time we will read and write the digits.

show.text: 8 = five and three more. 9 = five and four more, one away from ten. Next: reading and writing the digits.

notes.topic: Nine as one away from ten
